item.title: From Munhumutapa to Second Republic: A continuing legacy of trade, empowerment and unity @ZANUPF_Official
item.description: Rutendo Nyeve POLITICAL analysts have described the forthcoming Munhumutapa Day as a significant occasion that reflects how the Second Republic’s development trajectory and mantras are deeply rooted in the historic Munhumutapa State. As the nation prepares to commemorate this auspicious day on Tuesday, experts say the commemoration is not merely a historical reflection, but a reaffirmation of Zimbabwe’s enduring legacy of trade, empowerment, and self-determination. The historic Munhumutapa State was renowned as a powerful and sophisticated trading empire that engaged with the Portuguese and Chinese long before such interactions were common in the region. Analysts note that the Second Republic, under President Mnangagwa, mirrors this legacy through its Zimbabwe is Open for Business philosophy and its stance of being a friend to all and enemy to none. This strategic re-engagement with the global community echoes the entrepreneurial spirit of the Munhumutapa people. Political Scientist and ZANU PF Bulawayo Provincial Youth League Secretary for Information, Cde Addington Mpofu, emphasised this intrinsic link. Munhumutapa was a very powerful state, a historic state, a very important part of our history as a country. It was one of the earliest states to start trading, and it was arguably one of the biggest trading states in the Southern African region... because they were trading with the Portuguese, they were trading with the Chinese, said Cde Mpofu. So it is a very important part of our history because it shows us not only where we come from, but where we are headed and where we are. Right now we are saying Zimbabwe is open for business. We are saying ilizwe lakhiwa ngabanikazi balo (a nation is built by its own people). All these things that the President says today are embedded in the philosophy of Munhumutapa State. It’s a continuation. So we view the President as someone who has picked up the spear to finish the job here in Zimbabwe. Cde Mpofu further highlighted that the Second Republic’s empowerment initiatives are a modern translation of this legacy. He said youth-focused programmes, including the distribution of heifers, 10-hectare plots, and the US$200 000 capital injection per province enabled Bulawayo youth to procure three tipper trucks and get emancipated. As we approach Munhumutapa Day Commemorations 2026, we are reminded of the empowerment initiatives. We have the Munhumutapa youth housing scheme whereby we are going to benefit as young people and it’s going to be the biggest highlight of the 2026 commemorations, he said. The alignment of Munhumutapa Day with President Mnangagwa’s birthday further cements the narrative of a leadership destined to complete the historic mission of uniting and developing the nation. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: Family Voices win Best Acappella Award at INGOMAs
item.description: Mbulelo Mpofu, BULAWAYO-based vocal ensemble Family Voices has added another international accolade to its growing collection after their album, Evidence of the Kingdom, won the Best Acappella Award at the 13th Independent National Gospel Music Awards (INGOMAs) held at Glory House in Midrand, South Africa, recently. The group was the only Zimbabwean act represented at this year’s awards, giving it an opportunity to showcase the country’s gospel and a cappella music on an international platform. Family Voices spokesman Michael Sibanda said the award was a major milestone for the group, which has been pursuing vocal music for more than two decades. “Winning this award felt surreal. We were over the moon,” Sibanda said. He said the achievement reminded the group of its progress since representing Zimbabwe in the 2020 Old Mutual Amazing Voices competition, where it finished fourth. The latest recognition follows another successful outing at the Contemporary Acappella Recording Awards (CARA) in the United States, where Family Voices received 11 nominations and emerged first runner-up in six categories. “We feel like we are in the right direction, seeing as our album is gaining global recognition. We feel honoured to fly high the flag of Zimbabwe,” Sibanda said. He said the INGOMAs award was particularly important because a cappella music remained a relatively niche genre in the mainstream music industry. “This win means we are gradually breaking through into the international stages and getting the recognition we deserve. As far as a cappella is concerned, it is a genre which is not so popular in the music scene, and we feel this win is a step in the right direction through the gospel and secular circles,” he said. Sibanda said Evidence of the Kingdom was not only a musical project but also reflected the group’s Christian faith and its desire to positively influence society. “Evidence of the Kingdom isn’t only our album name. It’s also a message about the Kingdom of God we are living both in our individual lives and as a group,” he said. He also said that the group hoped to use its growing profile to inspire young people, particularly amid concerns over drug and alcohol abuse. “We intend to be a beacon of hope and say if we can rise above the challenges we face as a community, so can you. Through hard work and commitment and, above all, God ordering your footsteps, you can be what you want to become,” he said. Founded in 1999, Family Voices has established itself as one of Zimbabwe’s enduring vocal ensembles. Its former members include Mkhululi Bhebhe and the late Eric Moyo, who went on to become members of South Africa’s Joyous Celebration. The group has performed at platforms including the Harare International Festival of Arts, Essence Festival in Durban and Joyous Celebration shows. It has also shared stages with musicians such as the late Oliver Mtukudzi, Hugh Masekela, Judith Sephuma and Steve Dyer. The INGOMAs award marks another milestone in Family Voices’ journey to take Zimbabwean gospel and a cappella music to a wider international audience. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews

item.title: Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe launches awards to reward SMEs
item.description: Business Reporter STANBIC Bank Zimbabwe has launched ‘The Standard Bank Africa Business Awards’ aimed at celebrating and recognising exceptional small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across Africa. The Standard Bank Africa Business Awards are the first of their kind and seek to play a pivotal role in driving innovation, resilience, leadership and economic impact within industries and communities. Stanbic Bank head of business and commercial banking, Mr Patson Mahatchi, said the awards are open to eligible SMEs across Africa, including businesses that do not currently bank with Standard Bank Group or Stanbic Bank. Mr Mahatchi said the awards have been established to celebrate and recognise impactful businesses driving growth, innovation and excellence across the continent. The awards feature five categories designed to recognise excellence across key sectors and business segments, including: agriculture; construction; Fast Moving Consumer Goods and retail, manufacturing, women in business and youth-owned businesses. Mr Mahatchi said Stanbic Bank was honoured to celebrate the entrepreneurs, innovators, and business leaders who are shaping Zimbabwe’s economy and contributing to Africa’s growth story through the awards. He said Stanbic Bank is cognizant of the fact that small and medium-sized enterprises across Zimbabwe are creating jobs, developing innovative solutions, strengthening communities, and unlocking opportunities that drive sustainable economic growth. “At Stanbic Bank, we firmly believe that SMEs are the engine of economic development. Driven by our purpose; ‘Zimbabwe is Our Home, We Drive Her Growth’, we continue to support businesses with access to financial solutions, advisory services, market opportunities, and platforms that enable growth,” he said. Mr Mahatchi said The Africa Business Awards also seek to recognise and celebrate those businesses that demonstrate excellence, innovation, growth, and positive social impact. More importantly, these awards provide an opportunity for Zimbabwean businesses to gain continental recognition and showcase their achievements on a larger African stage. He said Stanbic Bank recognizes that extraordinary businesses already exist within Zimbabwe and that their stories deserve to be told. Their achievements deserve to be celebrated while their contribution to economic transformation deserve recognition. “We, therefore, encourage businesses from across Zimbabwe, regardless of size or sector, to participate in these awards,” said Mr Mahatchi, adding that participants can be drawn from those SMEs who would have pioneered innovation, expanded exports, empowered communities, embraced sustainability, or created employment among many others. He said Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe’s commitment extends beyond banking adding that the institution is committed to enabling growth, fostering entrepreneurship, and supporting the ambitions of businesses that will define Africa’s future. “These awards reflect that commitment. To all entrepreneurs and business owners, I encourage you to seize this opportunity, share your story, celebrate your achievements and inspire others. “Let Zimbabwe’s business excellence be represented among the very best on the continent,” said Mr Mahatchi. Stanbic Bank Zimbabwe head of enterprise banking, Sarah Charangwa said the awards are open to registered SMEs operating within eligible African markets where Standard Bank or Stanbic Bank has a presence. The group operates in 21 sub-Saharan African countries, including its anchor market of South Africa, plus countries such Angola, Kenya, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe. She said SMEs may enter multiple categories, provided that each submission is completed separately and meets the specific criteria for the relevant category. Businesses may enter the category that best aligns with their core business activities and demonstrated impact. Charangwa said entries will be assessed against criteria including: leadership and vision; innovation and creativity; sustainability and resilience; market and community impact; business growth and scalability as well as financial performance. “Entries will be reviewed by an independent panel comprising business leaders, industry experts, entrepreneurs and representatives from Standard Bank Group and partner organisations. Charangwa said winners stand to receive recognition, networking opportunities, funding, business exposure, mentorship opportunities and other benefits associated with the awards. “Startups may apply provided they are formally registered and able to demonstrate measurable business activity, innovation and growth potential,” she said. (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
